variants.headline: The colony has voted
variants.sub: The colony has held its election to the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
An election to the Colonial Assembly has been held in {colony}. The event places representation at the centre of public attention. The assessment of {target} should distinguish the holding of an election from any claim about what its result authorises.

Our movement regards representation as a duty, not a decoration to be worn until the next campaign. Our principles require political attention that keeps the purpose of public responsibility firmly in view here.

variants.headline: Ballots before the business of government
variants.sub: Voting in an election to the Colonial Assembly has taken place.
variants.body:
A ballot is a decision about representation, not a signed approval of every future measure. Following the election to the Colonial Assembly, that distinction deserves attention in any discussion of {target}. The colony has voted; political interpretation is a separate matter.

Our movement regards representation as a duty, not a decoration to be worn until the next campaign. Our principles require political attention that keeps the purpose of public responsibility firmly in view here.

variants.headline: An Assembly election enters the record
variants.sub: An election to the Colonial Assembly has been held in {colony}.
variants.body:
The election to the Colonial Assembly belongs in the colony's public record. Its meaning should be considered without supplying results or promises that this report does not contain. For {target}, the event invites scrutiny of the relationship between representation and responsibility.

Our movement regards representation as a duty, not a decoration to be worn until the next campaign. Our principles require political attention that keeps the purpose of public responsibility firmly in view here.
